_readme: Breaking changes that CANNOT be repaired automatically, in plain English.
This is the companion to META-INF/rewrite/botmaker-sdk.yml, and the division between them is the
point: the YAML is executable and holds everything a recipe can fix; this file is display text and
holds only what is left over. A change belongs here when no recipe can express the repair -- the
call site needs a decision from the person who wrote it (a new argument whose value depends on what
the bot is doing, a method whose semantics changed while its signature did not, a behaviour that
moved to a different class with different lifetime).
Inventing a format is appropriate here and nowhere else in this feature: there is no standard for
'sentences to show a user', and unlike the migration rules, nothing executes this.
It is read by two consumers:
- tools/check-api-rules.py, which treats an entry as coverage for a japicmp-reported break, so a
change that is genuinely unmigratable can still pass the build -- by being written down.
- Studio's upgrade report (Phase 4a), which prints 'summary' and 'action' verbatim.
'member' is matched against japicmp's report and must be exact:
This file grows only when something genuinely cannot be automated. If it is filling up faster than
botmaker-sdk.yml, the API changes are being designed without regard for the people running them.
